liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears Dupree's as a song that comes naturally to Jerry, and enjoys it greatly; Reviewer says Jerry fumbles lyrics in the second verse and the band seems ready to stop [24][26]
- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): Drums into Iko Iko into Eyes of the World sounds as if a drum corps is playing alongside the band; Second set features a long Iko Iko with lots of drums [16][27]
- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Jerry begins Eyes with the line about a creepy summer home, which the reviewer loves; Eyes is very unusual here because of all the extra people on stage [24][27]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer calls the opening China Cat into Rider decent, with some energy but average [26]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer finds Minglewood poorly placed and lacking intensity from the band [26]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer, after a rough psychedelic night, was finally able to stand up during Stella Blue [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Hey Bo Diddley**: back after 925 archived shows (4921 days); rare: 5 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-02-11.169567.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 137 min [1]
- **gd86-02-11.sbd.munder.11716.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 128 min; rated 4.21/5 by 19 [12]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the start of Truckin' came out bad in their download, though the overall sound is easy listening; Reviewer notes fun reverb and vocals on the recording; Reviewer calls it an excellent soundboard with a great bass line [16][19][23]
- **gd1986-02-11.135519.sbd.set2-pcm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 80 min [15]
- **gd1986-02-11.169566.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 22 songs; 137 min [2]

## Around the show

- Joseph Campbell, professor, author and Deadhead, was on stage with the band without playing [20]
- The Nevilles came out in headdress and sang a peacepipe song during the first set, per this reviewer [21]
- The Nevilles add a Cajun flavor to the second set [24]
- Most of the second set features members of the Neville Brothers, including Art Neville on keyboards and tambourine [1]
- Neville Brothers members joined for Drums, Iko Iko, Eyes, and the encore; Phil sat out the encore, Weir played tambourine [7]
- Most of the set had Neville Brothers members; the encore was without Phil, with Weir on tambourine [15]
- By 1986 the band's playing had become formulaic and boxed in; this show feels refreshing, with an unusual second-set arrangement [18]
- Reviewer sees this as supporting the view that 85/86 was among the last great touring years before the Dead got hugely popular [25]
- Of the five nights in this run, reviewer says this first set is the meatiest [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-02-11.169567.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Steve Marcus' Master Soundboard Cassettes > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell MX-90) [1]. Also: A PCM soundboard source from Charlie Miller supplies a 49-second patch in Space [1]
- **gd86-02-11.sbd.munder.11716.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> PCM> DAT> CD [12]
- **gd1986-02-11.135519.sbd.set2-pcm.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> PCM -> Dat [15]. Also: This is a 16-bit PCM soundboard source of the second set, coordinated by Miller [15]
- **gd1986-02-11.169566.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Steve Marcus' Master Soundboard Cassettes > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell MX-90) [2]
